issues.description: The manuscript contains a fundamental contradiction regarding the sample. The Abstract and Introduction claim a 'national probability sample' and 'general population sample,' but the Method section states participants were recruited from an 'introductory psychology participant pool at Victoria University of Wellington.'
issues.quote: We examine the longitudinal influence of SDO and RWA... in a national probability sample over five years. [Abstract] vs. We recruited participants through the introductory psychology participant pool at Victoria University of Wellington. [Method]

issues.description: The reported degrees of freedom (df = 2279) for the path analysis are mathematically impossible. For a model with 15 observed variables (3 variables across 5 time points), the maximum number of unique elements in the covariance matrix is 120 (15*16/2). The df cannot exceed this number.

A Chi-square value of 36,511.73 with a sample size of N=374 is extremely implausible for this type of model. Chi-square is generally a function of (N-1) * Fmin; such a high value suggests either a catastrophic model failure or a major reporting error.

The authors repeatedly claim the results are generalizable to the 'general population' and 'nationally representative,' yet the sample consists of 374 psychology students with an average age of 19. This is a convenience sample, not a representative one.
issues.quote: Our research uses a nationally representative sample, meaning that our results are highly generalisable, at least to the New Zealand population.

issues.description: The authors claim SDO is a 'stronger' predictor than RWA based on unstandardized coefficients, despite their own statistical test (constraining paths to equality) failing to reach significance (p = .126). A non-significant difference means they cannot claim one is stronger than the other.
issues.quote: We found that our original model provides comparable fit to the data 2(1) = 2.34, p = .126, but based on the pattern of unstandardized coefficients we interpret SDO as a stronger predictor

issues.description: The construct 'Environmentalism' is operationalized using only two items. Furthermore, the text refers to this variable interchangeably as 'environmentalism,' 'environmental concern,' and 'willingness to sacrifice,' which are distinct psychological constructs.
issues.quote: Environmentalism was measured as participants’ concern about environmental problems... 'How concerned are you about the current state of the natural environment?' and 'To what extent do you think environmental problems have been exaggerated?'

issues.description: The authors make strong causal claims ('causal pathway,' 'causal effect') based on cross-lagged panel models. While longitudinal, these data remain correlational and cannot rule out unmeasured third-variable causes or establish true causality.
issues.quote: These results suggest that there is a causal pathway from ideological attitudes to environmentalism.

issues.description: The study uses listwise deletion for a 5-wave longitudinal study. This is highly problematic as it significantly reduces power and assumes data are Missing Completely At Random (MCAR), which is rarely true in longitudinal research. No attrition analysis is provided.
issues.quote: Analyses were conducted using listwise deletion.

issues.description: The authors only report internal consistency (reliability) for Time 1. In a longitudinal study, reliability for all constructs at every time point must be reported to ensure measurement stability.
issues.quote: Table 1 presents the descriptive statistics and correlations between our variables at Time 1.

issues.description: The authors imposed a stationary model (constraining all paths to be equal across time) without first testing whether the data actually support stationarity. This can mask meaningful developmental changes or period effects.
issues.quote: We imposed this stationary cross-lagged model because we were more interested in the overall and comparative effects

issues.description: The text defines the significance threshold as p < .05, but the figure caption claims a threshold of p < .01.
issues.quote: we adopted a significance threshold of p < .05 [Results] vs. All meet our accepted threshold for significance of p < .01 [Figure 1]

issues.description: The analysis fails to include standard demographic covariates (e.g., gender, political orientation, income) which are known to correlate with both SDO/RWA and environmentalism, increasing the risk of spurious associations.
issues.quote: The model included three variables across five measurement points

issues.description: In the results text, the authors use 'SD' to refer to what is clearly the Standard Error (SE) of the B coefficient.
issues.quote: SDO was a stronger predictor of change in environmental sacrifice (B = -.11, SD = .01, p < .001)

issues.description: The authors note that one RWA item was missing at Time 2 but do not explain how this was handled in the path model (e.g., mean imputation, latent variable adjustment, or simply using a 5-item mean).
issues.quote: The item... was not assessed at time two, but included in all other time points.

issues.description: The text states that standardized parameters are presented, but Figure 1 is labeled as showing unstandardized parameters.
issues.quote: We present standardized parameters [Results] vs. Figure 1. Unstandardized parameters [Figure 1]

issues.description: The authors interpret the lack of a path from SDO to RWA as evidence that New Zealanders are 'socialized into authoritarianism to a greater extent,' which is a speculative leap not supported by the cross-lagged coefficients alone.
issues.quote: this suggests that New Zealander’s are socialized into authoritarianism to a greater extent than social dominance.

issues.description: The authors do not specify if they allowed for correlated residuals between the same items/constructs across time, which is standard practice in longitudinal path analysis to account for unique item variance.
issues.quote: We also constrained to equality the residual variance for the same item over time

issues.description: The reported Cronbach's alphas for SDO (.69) and RWA (.70) are at the very low end of acceptability, which increases measurement error and attenuates the observed longitudinal relationships.
issues.quote: Reliabilities for SDO and RWA were poorer than is typically the case... (.69 and .70)

issues.description: There is no mention of pre-registration for this study. Given the 'stationary' constraints and specific item selections, there is a risk of undisclosed researcher degrees of freedom in model specification.
issues.quote: We used path analysis to examine associations...

issues.description: The manuscript references the 'NZAVS' (New Zealand Attitudes and Values Study) and its website for sample details, but the NZAVS is a national probability sample of adults, whereas the Method section describes a local student pool. This suggests the authors may be mislabeling their data source.
issues.quote: Full details about the sample... are available on the NZAVS website.
